issues.description: play.ts changed from public import to internal source path and contains debug scaffolding
issues.detail: play.ts now imports from './packages/zod/src/index.js' and contains console.log debugging for a manual repro. This file appears to be a scratchpad that should not be committed in this state — it breaks any external consumer of play.ts and ships debug noise. Revert or exclude from the PR.

issues.description: Override invoked for both child and parent doubles user-visible override count (6 -> 12)
issues.detail: Removing the `if (!seen.isParent)` guard around `ctx.override` causes user-supplied override callbacks to fire once per node in the parent chain (test asserts 12 instead of 6). This is a breaking behavior change for anyone relying on overrides running once per logical schema; needs intentional design + changelog, not silent doubling.

issues.description: JSON.stringify equality for de-dup is fragile across key order and non-serializable values
issues.detail: Both de-dup branches compare via `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])`. Object key order, undefined values, functions, or NaN will produce false negatives/positives, leading to inconsistent omission of keys. Use a structural deep-equal or compare canonicalized forms.

issues.description: Parent-only property pruning may strip legitimate child fields named like parent keys
issues.detail: In the `isParentRef` branch, any key not in `_cached` is deleted. If the parent contributed semantically important fields (e.g., contentEncoding, type) that the child legitimately inherits and should expose, they are now removed unless re-set by the child. Combined with the file-processor change, this can drop properties consumers previously saw at the top level.

issues.description: z.file() snapshot loses string/length constraints from anyOf branches
issues.detail: The new file snapshot moves shared props to root but drops `type: string`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `contentEncoding`, `format` from each anyOf branch. Validators that evaluate each anyOf alternative in isolation (per JSON Schema semantics, type/length must match within the chosen branch) may now accept inputs that should be rejected. Confirm semantics intentionally changed.

issues.description: Recursive flattenRef on parent may re-enter and is order-sensitive
issues.detail: `flattenRef` is now invoked twice for a node when both `ref` and `parent` are set (`flattenRef(ref)` then `flattenRef(seen.parent)`), guarded only by `seen.ref === null`. The second call short-circuits, but the implicit ordering between processor-set ref and parent-set ref is subtle; add a comment or explicit guard documenting the invariant.

review.summary: The core change — tracking `parent` separately from processor-set `ref` and propagating $refs through wrappers — is a reasonable design and the new "describe with id on wrapper" test demonstrates a real fix. However, two issues should block merge: play.ts has been turned into a debug scratchpad pointing at internal paths, and the override callback now fires for every parent in the chain (test count doubled from 6 to 12), which is a behavior change for downstream users. Secondary concerns are the fragile JSON.stringify-based de-dup, aggressive parent-only key pruning, and a z.file() snapshot whose anyOf branches no longer carry per-branch type/length constraints.
